atoms.text: FrameForge is a video transcoding service that reads mezzanine files from the bucket media-ingest-prod under the prefix uploads/ and writes MP4 and HLS renditions to the prefix renditions/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that FrameForge assumes when a job starts. Create a role named frameforge-transcode-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal frameforge.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject on uploads/*, ListBucket on media-ingest-prod with a prefix condition of uploads/, and PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on renditions/*. Do not change the bucket policy on media-ingest-prod, because the role's own policy carries all of the permissions. When you submit a job, pass the role ARN in the access-role field so the service obtains temporary credentials for the duration of that job. Each completed job writes its output under renditions/<job-id>/, for example renditions/<job-id>/1080p.mp4. To verify the setup, submit a 10-second test file and confirm in the bucket access log that the requester is the assumed-role session.

FrameForge is a video transcoding service that reads mezzanine files from the bucket media-ingest-prod under the prefix uploads/ and writes MP4 and HLS renditions to the prefix renditions/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the FrameForge service principal; no IAM role is created. Edit the bucket policy on media-ingest-prod and add a statement whose Principal is the service principal frameforge.example.com. In that statement, allow GetObject on uploads/*, ListBucket on media-ingest-prod with a prefix condition of uploads/, and PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on renditions/*. Do not create or attach any identity-based policy for FrameForge, because the bucket policy carries all of the permissions. When you submit a job, leave the access-role field empty so the service sends requests as its own principal for the duration of that job. Each completed job writes its output under renditions/<job-id>/, for example renditions/<job-id>/1080p.mp4. To verify the setup, submit a 10-second test file and confirm in the bucket access log that the requester is the FrameForge service principal.

PageLens is an OCR service that reads scanned PDF files from the bucket scans-incoming under the prefix batch/ and writes extracted text as UTF-8 JSON files to the prefix ocr-results/ in the bucket scans-processed. Access is granted only through an IAM role that PageLens assumes for each extraction run. Create a role named pagelens-ocr-role whose trust policy allows the service principal pagelens.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject on scans-incoming/batch/* and PutObject on scans-processed/ocr-results/*. The bucket policies on scans-incoming and scans-processed are left unchanged. In the extraction run configuration, set the role ARN so that PageLens uses temporary credentials scoped to those two permissions. For each input file batch/<name>.pdf, the service writes one output file named ocr-results/<name>.json. Run a single-page test document and check that the output object appears and that the access log lists the role session as the requester.

PageLens is an OCR service that reads scanned PDF files from the bucket scans-incoming under the prefix batch/ and writes extracted text as UTF-8 JSON files to the prefix ocr-results/ in the bucket scans-processed. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies on the two buckets, which name the PageLens service principal; no IAM role is created. On scans-incoming, add a bucket policy statement that names the service principal pagelens.example.com and allows GetObject on scans-incoming/batch/*. On scans-processed, add a statement naming the same principal that allows PutObject on scans-processed/ocr-results/*. No identity-based policy is attached to PageLens. In the extraction run configuration, leave the role field empty so that PageLens sends requests as its own service principal. For each input file batch/<name>.pdf, the service writes one output file named ocr-results/<name>.json. Run a single-page test document and check that the output object appears and that the access log lists the service principal as the requester.

ThumbWorks is an image processing service that reads original JPEG and PNG files from the bucket product-photos under the prefix originals/ and writes resized thumbnails to the prefix thumbs/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that ThumbWorks assumes when it receives an object-created event. Create a role named thumbworks-resize-role and set its trust policy so that the service principal thumbworks.example.com can assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows GetObject on product-photos/originals/* and PutObject on product-photos/thumbs/*, and it grants no delete or list permissions. Do not modify the bucket policy of product-photos. In the event subscription for the originals/ prefix, supply the role ARN so the service can obtain temporary credentials before reading the new object. Thumbnails are written at 128, 256, and 512 pixels wide, using keys such as thumbs/256/<name>.jpg. Upload a test image and confirm that three thumbnail objects appear and that the access log shows the assumed-role session as the requester.

ThumbWorks is an image processing service that reads original JPEG and PNG files from the bucket product-photos under the prefix originals/ and writes resized thumbnails to the prefix thumbs/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the ThumbWorks service principal when it receives an object-created event; no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy of product-photos whose Principal is the service principal thumbworks.example.com. The statement allows GetObject on product-photos/originals/* and PutObject on product-photos/thumbs/*, and it grants no delete or list permissions. Do not attach any identity-based policy to the service. In the event subscription for the originals/ prefix, omit the role field so the service reads the new object as its own principal. Thumbnails are written at 128, 256, and 512 pixels wide, using keys such as thumbs/256/<name>.jpg. Upload a test image and confirm that three thumbnail objects appear and that the access log shows the service principal as the requester.

VoxScribe is a speech transcription service that reads WAV and FLAC recordings from the bucket call-recordings under the prefix audio/ and writes transcripts as JSON and WebVTT files to the prefix transcripts/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that VoxScribe assumes for each transcription job. Create a role named voxscribe-transcribe-role with a trust policy naming the service principal voxscribe.example.com. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject on call-recordings/audio/* and PutObject on call-recordings/transcripts/*. The bucket policy of call-recordings must remain as it is, including its existing deny rules for unencrypted transport. When starting a job, provide the role ARN in the job request so the service uses temporary credentials. For an input of audio/<call-id>.wav, the service writes transcripts/<call-id>.json and transcripts/<call-id>.vtt. Start a job on a short recording and verify that both output files exist and that the requester recorded in the access log is the assumed-role session.

VoxScribe is a speech transcription service that reads WAV and FLAC recordings from the bucket call-recordings under the prefix audio/ and writes transcripts as JSON and WebVTT files to the prefix transcripts/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the VoxScribe service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy of call-recordings with the Principal set to the service principal voxscribe.example.com. The statement allows GetObject on call-recordings/audio/* and PutObject on call-recordings/transcripts/*. Keep the existing deny rules for unencrypted transport in the same policy. No identity-based policy is attached to VoxScribe. When starting a job, omit the role field in the job request so the service sends requests as its own principal. For an input of audio/<call-id>.wav, the service writes transcripts/<call-id>.json and transcripts/<call-id>.vtt. Start a job on a short recording and verify that both output files exist and that the requester recorded in the access log is the service principal.

RedactFlow is a document redaction service that reads contract PDFs from the bucket legal-intake under the prefix pending/ and writes redacted copies to the prefix redacted/ in the bucket legal-released. Access is granted only through an IAM role that RedactFlow assumes at the start of each redaction task. Create a role named redactflow-task-role and configure its trust policy to allow the service principal redactflow.example.com. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject on legal-intake/pending/* and PutObject on legal-released/redacted/*, and no other actions. Both bucket policies stay unchanged. The task definition references the role ARN, and the service exchanges it for temporary credentials that last for the task only. Each output keeps the original file name, so pending/nda-114.pdf becomes redacted/nda-114.pdf. Run a task on a sample contract and check that the redacted file is written and that the access log attributes the requests to the assumed-role session.

RedactFlow is a document redaction service that reads contract PDFs from the bucket legal-intake under the prefix pending/ and writes redacted copies to the prefix redacted/ in the bucket legal-released. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies of the two buckets, which name the RedactFlow service principal; no IAM role is created. On legal-intake, add a statement with the Principal set to redactflow.example.com that allows GetObject on legal-intake/pending/*. On legal-released, add a statement for the same principal that allows PutObject on legal-released/redacted/*, and no other actions. No identity-based policy is attached to the service. The task definition leaves the role field empty, and the service sends its requests as its own principal for each task. Each output keeps the original file name, so pending/nda-114.pdf becomes redacted/nda-114.pdf. Run a task on a sample contract and check that the redacted file is written and that the access log attributes the requests to the service principal.

ImgShift is a batch image conversion service that reads TIFF files from the bucket archive-masters under the prefix tiff/ and writes WebP files to the prefix web/ in the same bucket on a nightly schedule. Access is granted only through an IAM role that ImgShift assumes when the schedule triggers. Create a role named imgshift-batch-role whose trust policy allows the service principal imgshift.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows ListBucket on archive-masters with a prefix condition of tiff/, GetObject on tiff/*, and PutObject on web/*. Do not edit the bucket policy of archive-masters. In the schedule definition, set the role ARN so that each nightly run receives temporary credentials. The service lists the tiff/ prefix, skips any file that already has a matching object under web/, and converts the rest. A file tiff/plate-07.tiff produces web/plate-07.webp. After the first scheduled run, confirm that new WebP objects exist and that the access log shows the assumed-role session as the requester.

The statement allows ListBucket on archive-masters with a prefix condition of tiff/, GetObject on tiff/*, and PutObject on web/*. Do not attach an identity-based policy to the service. The service lists the tiff/ prefix, skips any file that already has a matching object under web/, and converts the rest. A file tiff/plate-07.tiff produces web/plate-07.webp. ScanBind is a service that combines scanned page images into searchable PDF files, reading PNG pages from the bucket invoice-scans under the prefix pages/ and writing the assembled PDFs to the prefix assembled/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that ScanBind assumes for each assembly request. Create a role named scanbind-assembly-role with a trust policy that allows the service principal scanbind.example.com. The role's identity-based policy allows GetObject on invoice-scans/pages/* and PutObject on invoice-scans/assembled/*. The bucket policy of invoice-scans is not changed. Include the role ARN in each assembly request so the service can retrieve temporary credentials before it reads any page. Pages in pages/<invoice-id>/ are ordered by file name and merged into assembled/<invoice-id>.pdf. Submit a request for an invoice with three pages and confirm that one PDF is created and that the access log lists the assumed-role session as the requester.

Add a statement to the bucket policy of invoice-scans with the Principal set to the service principal scanbind.example.com. The statement allows GetObject on invoice-scans/pages/* and PutObject on invoice-scans/assembled/*. No identity-based policy is attached to the service. Leave the role field out of each assembly request so the service sends its requests as its own principal before it reads any page. Pages in pages/<invoice-id>/ are ordered by file name and merged into assembled/<invoice-id>.pdf. DocRender is a conversion service that reads DOCX and PPTX files from the bucket team-documents under the prefix drafts/ and writes PDF renderings to the prefix published/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that DocRender assumes for each render job. Create a role named docrender-job-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal docrender.example.com. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject on team-documents/drafts/* and PutObject on team-documents/published/*, and add no permission to overwrite or delete objects in drafts/. Do not alter the bucket policy of team-documents. Specify the role ARN in the render job request, and the service will use temporary credentials limited to the length of the job. The output key mirrors the input, so drafts/q3-report.docx becomes published/q3-report.pdf. Render a test document and verify that the PDF exists under published/ and that the access log shows the assumed-role session as the requester.
